key_insight: Matrix-structured optimizers like SOAP and SOAP-Muon can train ML interatomic potentials faster and more accurately than Adam, making optimizer choice a major but underused design lever.
engineering_relevance: For scientific ML workflows, swapping the default optimizer may improve convergence and label efficiency without changing the underlying NequIP or Allegro model architecture.
method: Implemented and compared Adam, Muon, SOAP, and SOAP-Muon
Trained NequIP and Allegro MLIP models with each optimizer
Evaluated convergence speed and final accuracy, including partial force supervision settings
evidence_signal: The abstract reports systematic comparisons showing SOAP and SOAP-Muon consistently outperform Adam, with the largest gains under partial force supervision.
watch_item: Matrix-structured optimizers may be more implementation-sensitive than Adam, so reproducibility and hyperparameter tuning should be checked carefully when transferring results.
paper_title: Beyond Adam: SOAP and Muon for Faster, Label-Efficient Training of Machine Learning Interatomic Potentials
